newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas halts airliner plans - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas halts airliner plans - WSJ.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp has foregone plans to build its largest and longest-range airliner, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
The newspaper scited "people familiar with" the company's decision as saying senior management decided to drop plans to build MD-XX on Friday.
It said it could not reach company officials to comment on the decision, which was not made public.
Also on Friday, McDonnell Douglas announced the resignation of Herbert Lanese, who had been in charge of its military aircraft division.

The newspaper said industry observers interpreted the resignation and the decision to not build the $2 billion plane -- at least not in the near future -- as perhaps part of a larger strategy to reshuffle senior management or plan a merger, among other things.
The airliner, which would have had a capacity of up to 375 passengers, was seen as an integral part of the company's efforts to develop a new line of planes, it added.
